html:
Duke of Normandy from 1035 and the first Norman king of England, from 1066 until his death in 1087. He was the illegitimate son of Duke Robert I and survived a dangerous childhood among feuding barons to become a hard, able ruler.

He claimed the English throne, saying his cousin Edward the Confessor had promised it to him. When Edward died in January 1066 and Harold Godwinson was crowned, William invaded. He beat and killed Harold at the Battle of Hastings on 14 October 1066 and was crowned in Westminster Abbey on Christmas Day.

As king he:

  • crushed revolts, above all in the "Harrying of the North" of 1069 to 1070, which laid waste to much of Yorkshire;
  • gave English lands to his Norman followers, so that within twenty years the old English nobility was nearly gone;
  • built castles, among them the Tower of London;
  • ordered the Domesday Book of 1086, a survey of land and wealth.

The Normans descended from Viking settlers in France. The Norman Conquest tied England to France for centuries.
